candidate.educational_objective: Apply the cited evidence to recognize the uniquely safest or most accurate nursing response in the clinical situation tested by V2-Q0116.

options.A: Perform hand hygiene and insert the catheter aseptically using sterile gloves, a sterile catheter kit, and a single-use lubricant packet.
options.B: Use sterile gloves and a sterile catheter but clean lubricant because the urethral meatus is colonized and cannot be made completely sterile.
options.C: Use clean gloves with a sterile catheter kit because only the catheter itself needs to remain sterile during insertion in an acute-care setting.
options.D: Use sterile insertion technique but disconnect the drainage tubing briefly after placement to verify urine flow before closing the system

candidate.rationale: CDC recommends that acute-care urinary catheters be inserted using aseptic technique and sterile equipment. Recommended supplies include sterile gloves, drape and sponges, appropriate antiseptic or sterile solution for periurethral cleaning, and a single-use lubricant packet. A closed drainage system should then be maintained.
candidate.source_claim_supported: In acute care, use aseptic insertion and sterile equipment, including sterile gloves and a single-use lubricant packet.
candidate.source_locator: CAUTI Summary of Recommendations — Appropriate urinary catheter insertion: aseptic technique and sterile equipment; single-use lubricant packet
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.stem: An indwelling urinary catheter is being inserted in an acute-care hospital. Which technique best reflects CDC CAUTI-prevention guidance?
